subject: Multi-point regional pinning: APAC edge + EU/US burst sizing request
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Kai Park <kai@helix.ai>, Jordan Li <jordan.li@helix.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Multi-point regional pinning: APAC edge + EU/US burst sizing request

Hi Kai / Jordan —

Thanks for the great convo yesterday. Helix's projected ramp in APAC and SEA looks promising and we'd like to propose a multipoint pinning approach to keep latency predictable while allowing cost-efficient burst capacity out of EU/US. Before we lock in numbers for a Dedicated pool commitment, I need the following from your side this week so we can size a recommended tranche: 

- Expected steady-state QPS (text gen calls) in APAC 00:00-08:00 UTC and peak window 08:00-16:00 UTC (per-hour average is fine)
- Percent of requests requiring long-context >2k tokens vs short-context <512 tokens
- Target p95 latency SLO per request (for split small vs large requests)
- Any compliance constraints (data residency, contract language for EU customers)

I've attached our regional_capacity_model_v2.xlsx with a first-pass table of GPU hours, expected token mix, and price/commit bands. If you can fill the highlighted columns (tab: Helix_input) we'll run a tranche-fit and propose a three-month and twelve-month commit scenario.

Next steps I propose:
1) You send the QPS + token mix by EOD Thursday (6/17)
2) We return a recommended APAC pool + EU/US burst plan with cost delta and fallback model variants by Friday (6/18)
3) If numbers look good, Ben will share the PO template and we can sign a starter tranche for July.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — want to lock capacity ahead of the Singapore Q4 procurement sprints.

Best,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: regional_capacity_model_v2.xlsx (Excel, 1.1MB)]

From: Kai Park <kai@helix.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Li <jordan.li@helix.ai>, procurement@helix.ai
Date: 2026-06-15T11:03:00+08:00
Subject: Re: Multi-point regional pinning: APAC edge + EU/US burst sizing request

Thanks Soojin —

We can get a preliminary QPS/time-of-day profile together. A few clarifying points from our side: 

- Our APAC traffic is very spiky for the next 6 weeks due to localized feature tests; steady-state daytime QPS could be ~350 req/s but spikes to ~1.2k req/s for 20-30 minute windows.
- Long-context usage is currently ~18% of calls but those calls are responsible for ~55% of our token consumption.
- Internal product target is p95 <= 350ms for short requests and p95 <= 700ms for long requests.
- For EU customers we need to ensure EU-residency for logs and audit trails — can Redwood provide separate retention/route for EU sessions?

I took a quick look at the attached model and I'll fill Helix_input with our best estimates by Thursday. One ask: please include an explicit fallback plan if APAC capacity is exhausted (e.g., route to EU with quantized variant).

—Kai
Kai Park
Head of Platform Engineering, Helix.ai

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Kai Park <kai@helix.ai>, Jordan Li <jordan.li@helix.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-16T07:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-point regional pinning: APAC edge + EU/US burst sizing request

Kai — thanks, that's exactly the level of detail we need. I filled the model with two scenarios attached:

- Scenario A (conservative): reserve 24xA100-equivalent GPUs in APAC with autoscale-burst to EU (quantized gpt variants) for 4x peak spikes.
- Scenario B (aggressive): reserve 48xA100-equivalent GPUs in APAC; smaller EU reserve, higher cost but less cross-region egress.

Quick notes:
- For long-context requests we recommend pinning to instances with larger KV-cache and enabling 8-bit quantization for the EU fallback to keep p95 under 900ms in worst cases.
- Yes — we can set EU routing to write-only logs to an EU KMS namespace and retain session events for 30 days; we'll surface the retention policy in the contract appendix.

I've attached the updated workbook (regional_capacity_model_v2.xlsx) with the two tranche proposals and a simple cost delta table (tab: overview). Please review the assumptions (cells highlighted in yellow) and let us know which scenario you'd prefer.

If you prefer, we can run a short load test next week from your APAC endpoints to validate p95s on our target hardware.

Soojin
[Attachment: regional_capacity_model_v2.xlsx (updated, Excel, 1.3MB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Kai Park <kai@helix.ai>
Date: 2026-06-16T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-point regional pinning: APAC edge + EU/US burst sizing request

Looping in a short finance/commit note —

Soojin, Kai: the two scenarios have materially different revenue and utilization profiles. Operationally we prefer Scenario A (smaller reserve + higher burst) because it lets us pack other tenants into leftover capacity and reduces stranded commitment risk. Commercially we can offer a stepped discount if Helix signs a 12-month commit with a 3-month ramp clause:

- 3-month starter tranche: 24 A100-eq reserve in APAC, month-to-month billing at list price
- 12-month commit: step-down unit price by 18% once committed (retroactive from contract start)

Ben — can you prepare the starter PO and include the 12-month commit appendix language? Kai, if procurement signs the starter PO we can schedule a July 1st provisioning.

Karthik
VP, Dedicated Capacity, Redwood

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kai Park <kai@helix.ai>, procurement@helix.ai
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-17T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: PO and starter tranche details (HLX-3279)

Hi Kai / procurement —

Attached is the starter PO template for the 3-month APAC starter tranche (24 A100-eq reserve). Key commercial bullets: 
- Starter tranche term: 3 months (provision on July 1)
- Billing: monthly in arrears, standard net30
- Onboarding credits: one-time provisioning credit of $8,000 applied to month 1
- Appendix: 12-month commit option with 18% step-down pricing and a 3-month ramp clause

I've included the PO as po_template_redwood.pdf (fillable). Please review and return signed by EOD Friday 6/18 if you want the July 1 start. If you need a revised appendix for data residency language, let me know and we'll have legal loop in.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Head of Sales Operations
[Attachment: po_template_redwood.pdf (PDF, 220KB)]

From: Kai Park <kai@helix.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Li <jordan.li@helix.ai>, procurement@helix.ai, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-18T14:30:00+08:00
Subject: Re: PO and starter tranche details (HLX-3279)

Ben / team —

Appreciate the clear options. Procurement will review the PO and the commit appendix; we expect to return a signed starter PO by close of business Friday (6/18) — will confirm with a signed copy or redlines. A couple clarifications we requested to legal (cc'd):
- Insert a short appendix clarifying EU log retention and KMS binding for EU-resident customers.
- Add a clause describing automatic fallback ordering if APAC pool is saturated (we prefer soft-fallback to EU quantized variants first).

Jonas / Soojin: once we sign, can Redwood provision a staging pool for the load test on June 24-25? That will help validate the p95s against our production mix.

I'll follow up with procurement and drop the signed PO into the HubSpot record once complete.

—Kai
